  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION MAYOR ZUCKERMAN SO ORDERED.

  MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN noted that he thought this event would be a
  wonderful addition to the City which will take place on Saturday, September 24.
  He then thanked the Rotary Club for their community involvement.

  In response to COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL, Dave Behar, ION Network Chief
  Executive, noted that registration is available at ridewiththetide.org.

F.  PROPOSAL TO CONDUCT AN INITIAL STUDY AND MITIGATED NEGATIVE
  DECLARATION FOR THE PALOS VERDES PIPELINE PROJECT; APPLICANT:
  CALIFORNIA WATER SERVICES COMPANY (CAL WATER); LOCATION: VARIOUS
  LOCATIONS CITY-WIDE

  Recommendation: That the City Council authorize the contract with ESA PCR in
  the amount of $93,230 to prepare the Initial Study and resulting, appropriate
  environmental determination for the Palos Verdes Pipeline Project.

  Senior Planner Naughton provided a staff report (as per agenda material).

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL inquired about the route for the east/west section
  of the pipeline and asked for clarification regarding the section that goes behind
  the Botanic Garden.

  Planning Director Wahba noted that this portion is in the horse trail parallel to
  the Botanic Garden south of the Garden.

  Senior Planner Naughton noted that there are several alignment alternatives and
  once the firm is chosen, Cal Water is open to optimization in an effort to make the
  alignments more efficient. Additionally, she noted that easements across 26
  private properties would be required.

  In response to COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL, Senior Planner Naughton noted that
  all the alternatives will be reflected in the initial study.

  MAYOR ZUCKERMAN stated that the original alignment proposal was not
  supported by the COUNCIL due to traffic impact concerns which is why the
  alignment goes through the Dapplegray neighborhood and the horse trails.
CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
SEPTEMBER 13, 2016
   MAYOR ZUCKERMAN commented that an evaluation would have to be made
  regarding the question of toxics due to the landfill being in close proximity.

  Planning Director Wahba noted that he will discuss this issue with Cal Water and
  their consultant.

  Senior Planner Naughton noted that air quality issues may require a detailed
  health risk analysis. She further noted that the traffic impact analysis would be
  handled under a separate scope.

  In regards to the toxic question, Senior Planner Naughton stated an additional
  scope of service may be required.

  Planning Director Wahba suggested that staff can contact the Department of Toxic
  Substances Control (DTSC) and obtain their comments as to what could be within
  the vicinity of the trail and see what they recommend.

  MAYOR ZUCKERMAN inquired if the selected firm has provided environmental
  review before for Cal Water and wanted to make sure they act in the City’s best
  interest.

  Planning Director Wahba provided a brief history of this firm.

  John Collazo, Project Manager, Palos Verdes Pipeline Project, responded that ESA
  PCR has been retained before on other projects. He noted that the firm comes
  highly recommended and has been carefully vetted. He further noted that he was
  confident they could execute this project.

  In response to MAYOR ZUCKERMAN, Senior Planner Naughton noted that a
  Request for Proposal had been sent out and a portion of the design plans should
  be available by December. Additionally, she stated that further information will
  be brought back to the COUNCIL at the next meeting.

  COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL

  TO CONTINUE THIS ITEM TO THE NEXT COUNCIL MEETING OF
  SEPTEMBER 27, 2016.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION MAYOR ZUCKERMAN SO ORDERED.

  MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN noted that he was not familiar with this firm and
  the COUNCIL should review this information carefully.

  COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ noted her understanding that if the COUNCIL enters
  into this agreement, the City will act as lead agency for the environmental review
  which will give the COUNCIL substantial authority over the issue of alignment
  among others.

G.  SALARY ADMINISTRATION POLICIES AND PROCEDURES

  Recommendation: That the City Council retain Management Partners for a study

H.  CREDIT CARD IMPLEMENTATION
